name: DAVIS: Planning Agent with Knowledge Graph-Powered Inner Monologue
venue: EMNLP 2025 Findings (Findings of the Association for Computational Linguistics: EMNLP 2025, pages 16490-16505; DOI 10.18653/v1/2025.findings-emnlp.895). Preprint arXiv:2410.09252 (cs.CL), submitted 11 Oct 2024 (v1), last revised 17 Sep 2025 (v2).
authors_affiliation: Minh Pham-Dinh (Davis Institute for Artificial Intelligence, Colby College), Munira Syed (University of Notre Dame), Michael Yankoski (Colby College / William & Mary), Trenton W. Ford (William & Mary). Correspondence: mhpham26@colby.edu. Funded in part by DARPA / Accelerate Foundation Models Research.
maintained_repo_url: https://github.com/minhphd/DAVIS (official code + prompts, MIT license; 6 commits, last updated Sep 2025; noted as potentially unstable due to dependency drift, cleanup ongoing). Not a leaderboard/paper-list; minimally maintained.
task_domain: Embodied/interactive decision-making and planning (text-based scientific agent in ScienceWorld), plus multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MusiqueQA) used to evaluate the World Model component.
problem_setting: Interactive, single-agent, model-based planning in a partially observable text environment, formalized as a POMDP P=(S,A,T,R,Omega,O,gamma). The agent must complete grade-school science tasks in ScienceWorld (e.g., melting/boiling, building circuits, growing plants) requiring multi-hop scientific reasoning, temporal/structured understanding of an evolving environment, safety/interpretability, and operation under partial observability. Supervision is provided as golden trajectories used offline to populate memory: all RAG-based agents (DAVIS, RAP) are initialized with five episodes of golden-trajectory rollouts per task variation (a total of 150 training variations); evaluation uses three randomly sampled test variations per task (90 test variations total). The agent maintains an approximate belief state b_hat_t = f(trajectory history) updated recurrently, and plans inside a learned/retrieval-augmented World Model before acting in the environment. The World Model alone is also evaluated as a standalone multi-hop QA system on HotpotQA and MusiqueQA (400 sampled instances each).
what_is_retrieved: Past experiences/transitions stored as a temporal knowledge graph (TKG): retrieved units are temporally-ordered subgraphs of (entity, relation, entity, timestamp) tuples extracted from past (observation, action, next-observation) transitions. During the inner monologue, the agent retrieves relevant subgraphs via graph QA to predict next observations/rewards and to fill knowledge gaps for planning.
retrieval_grounding: HYBRID toward GROWING/episodic structured memory. The retrievable store is a Temporal Knowledge Graph (World Model) that the agent itself constructs from its own past experience transitions; it is populated offline from golden-trajectory rollouts (training phase) and is intended to evolve with the agent's interactions ('continuously evolves with the agent's interactions'). It is not a static external document/KB corpus; it is an agent-built experiential memory.
completeness_vs_topk_objective: Not a fixed top-k ranking objective. Retrieval narrows to relevant entity types, selects the two most relevant entities, then iteratively expands their neighbors to form a maximal subgraph (aiming for a feasible/complete temporal path rather than a ranked list), reordering edges by timestamp to recover the complete sequence of events. The objective is coverage of the causally/temporally relevant subgraph (a feasible path), not a fixed-size ranked retrieval; entity scope is capped at two seed entities for tractability.
cbr_cycle_coverage: N/A (not framed as case-based reasoning). If mapped loosely: Retrieve (subgraph retrieval via graph QA) and Retain (writing transitions into the TKG) are present; there is no discrete case Reuse/Revise of stored cases as case-based-reasoning units. Use a 4-flag interpretation: [Retrieve: yes (subgraph), Reuse: partial (informs transition/reward prediction), Revise: no (no case adaptation), Retain: yes (TKG write of transitions)].
explicit_cbr_grounding: False. The work does not frame itself as case-based reasoning and does not cite Aamodt & Plaza / Kolodner. It is positioned as model-based planning with a temporal-knowledge-graph World Model and an agentic multi-turn (inner-monologue) retrieval system, contrasted against vector-based RAG (Reflexion, RAP).
retrieval_unit: KG-subgraph: a temporally-ordered maximal subgraph of (entity, relation, entity, timestamp) tuples retrieved from a Temporal Knowledge Graph. The underlying stored units are quadruples (v_i, e_j, v_k, tau) extracted from concatenated transitions (o_t || a_t || o_{t+1}).
index_source: Growing experiential memory, offline-induced then evolving: the TKG World Model is built from the agent's own past transitions. It is populated during a training phase from five episodes of golden-trajectory rollouts across 150 task variations (offline construction), and is designed to continuously evolve with interactions. Not a static external corpus.
index_structure_topology: Knowledge GRAPH (temporal knowledge graph). Entities are nodes; typed relations are edges; each edge carries a timestamp tau encoding when the fact was introduced. Stored in PostgreSQL (per the code). Retrieval first restricts to relevant entity types (e.g., PER, LOC), then does neighbor expansion to form a maximal subgraph, then temporal edge reordering.
retriever_type: LLM-as-retriever / graph QA (agentic). Retrieval is performed by a graph-QA function (graphQA(q)) that an LLM drives: it selects entity types, picks the two most relevant entities, expands neighbors into a subgraph, temporally reorders edges, and passes the temporal sequence to an LLM as in-context examples for extrapolation/summarization. No dense vector or BM25 retriever over the experience store; explicitly contrasted with vector-based retrieval (RAP, Reflexion). KG construction uses LLaMA3-70B-Instruct + Stanford CoreNLP coreference resolution.
retriever_learning_signal: None (off-the-shelf / prompted). The retriever is not trained; it is a prompted LLM graph-QA process. There is no contrastive, RL, or preference-learning signal for retrieval. Entity-type narrowing, entity selection, neighbor expansion, and temporal reordering are heuristic/prompt-driven; the LLM extrapolates over temporal patterns in-context (citing Lee et al. 2023 on TKG forecasting with in-context learning).
query_construction: Thought-conditioned / agent-initiated queries. During transition prediction the World Model's transition/reward predictors emit a query q (e.g., 'Where can I find water?') when they detect a knowledge gap; this question is the retrieval query. The query is then expanded inside graph QA (entity-type narrowing -> two-entity selection -> subgraph neighbor expansion -> temporal reordering). Belief state b_hat_t = f(trajectory history) is maintained and conditions the queries.
query_granularity: Step/state-level with an inner inner-loop: queries are generated per planning step during transition prediction (Algorithm 2), and multiple queries can be issued within a single transition prediction via the multi-turn inner monologue (up to Maximum QA Turns = 5). Effectively two-level: per-step planning plus per-monologue-turn sub-queries.
when_to_retrieve: Iterative / active (agent-initiated, multi-turn). Retrieval is triggered as an inner monologue loop during transition/reward prediction: while i<k or not predicted, the transition and reward models may emit a query q; if q is non-empty, graph QA is invoked and the (q, answer) pair is appended to the running monologue M. This continues up to k=5 maximum QA turns or until a prediction is reached.
retrieval_trigger_signal: Agent-initiated request driven by detected knowledge gaps. In Algorithm 2 the transition/reward predictors return a query q together with a tentative prediction; a non-empty q (i.e., the LLM signals it still needs information / a remaining knowledge gap) triggers another graph-QA retrieval turn. The loop also terminates on a fixed budget (k = Maximum QA Turns = 5) or once a confident prediction ('predicted') is produced. So: hybrid of self-detected uncertainty/knowledge-gap signal plus a fixed turn-budget cap.
reranking: No explicit learned reranking stage. Within retrieval, edges of the retrieved maximal subgraph are temporally reordered (sorted by timestamp) to establish a coherent event sequence before being passed to the LLM; this is temporal ordering rather than relevance reranking. Entity selection ('two most relevant entities') is a coarse relevance filter performed by the LLM, not a cross-encoder reranker.
retrieved_context_refinement: Decompose-then-recompose + summarization: the retrieved maximal subgraph is temporally reordered into a coherent event sequence, then passed to an LLM as in-context examples for extrapolation and summarization to generate a structured, interpretable natural-language response. Multi-turn inner monologue accumulates (query, answer) pairs that progressively refine the predicted transition/reward before planning. The Critic additionally refines plans post-execution via reflection.
tool_document_engineering: N/A (no tool/skill retrieval; retrieval is over an experiential temporal knowledge graph, not tool documentation).
index_content_separation: Partial: the lightweight retrievable index is the temporal knowledge graph (entities/relations/timestamps); the heavier raw transition text is summarized at write time into KG tuples, so retrieval operates over a compact structured graph rather than raw trajectory text. Not a formal progressive-disclosure SOP-index-then-content protocol.
dynamic_index_and_protocol: N/A (no external tool index/integration protocol such as RapidAPI/MCP/function-calling for tools). The TKG is built and queried via an internal graph-QA pipeline (LLaMA3-70B extraction + Stanford CoreNLP coreference, PostgreSQL store).
tool_dependency_awareness: N/A (no inter-tool dependency modeling). The graph models inter-entity relations and temporal ordering of events/transitions, not tool-to-tool dependencies.
how_retrieved_used: Prompt augmentation for model-based planning. Retrieved temporal subgraphs (summarized via graph QA into the inner monologue M_t) are injected as context into the World Model's policy pi(a_t | b_hat_t, M_t), transition model T_hat(o_{t+1} | b_hat_t, a_t, M_t), and reward model R_hat(r_t | b_hat_t, a_t, M_t). The WM uses them to approximate future observations/rewards and to generate a high-level natural-language plan/trajectory tau_{t:t+L}, which the Actor decomposes into executable low-level commands and the Critic validates against actual outcomes.
planning_integration: Retrieve-then-plan inside a model-based planning loop with replanning. The agent runs Algorithm 1 (Planning with Retrieval-Augmented World Model): estimate state -> select action via policy -> predict next observation/reward via Transition Prediction (Algorithm 2, which itself runs the multi-turn inner-monologue retrieval) -> append to trajectory -> optional safety check. A predicted trajectory of length L (=5) is generated, then handed to an Actor (decomposes into low-level executable commands and executes step by step) and a Critic (compares predicted vs actual transitions; on significant deviation updates a reflection list and triggers replanning of the subtask). Retrieval is woven into per-step transition prediction during planning.
reasoning_search_interleaving_granularit: Per-step (per planning/transition-prediction step), with a nested per-monologue-turn granularity: within each transition prediction the inner monologue interleaves up to 5 query/answer retrieval turns with reasoning before committing a predicted (observation, reward). Plan-level retrieval feeds into per-step actor execution and critic-triggered replanning.
adaptation_mechanism: N/A as CBR case adaptation. Closest mechanism: execution-feedback-driven revision via the Critic, which compares predicted vs actual (o,r,o') transitions, produces a qualitative discrepancy score Delta_t, appends reflections to R_t, and triggers replanning of the subtask (e.g., 'find an alternative heating method' when a stove is broken). This is plan revision via reflection, not retrieved-case adaptation.
retrieved_item_representation: Structured note distilled into free text: the retrieved temporal subgraph is summarized by an LLM into a coherent, structured, interpretable natural-language answer that becomes a (query, answer) entry in the inner monologue. The World Model's output plan is itself a high-level, interpretable natural-language trajectory. Underlying stored form is structured KG quadruples (entity, relation, entity, timestamp).
abstraction_level_of_retrieved_unit: State-aware / temporally-structured experiential knowledge: retrieved units are temporally-ordered subgraphs of past transitions (causal/temporal event sequences), more abstract and structured than a raw trajectory but grounded in concrete past experience. They are extrapolated by the LLM into predicted next states, i.e., reusable temporal patterns rather than verbatim demonstrations or distilled high-level strategies.
noise_robustness_mechanism: Critic-based self-reflection/validation: the LLM Critic checks semantic consistency between predicted and actual transitions and triggers replanning on significant deviation, guarding against erroneous WM predictions. Retrieval scope is constrained (two seed entities, relevant entity types) to limit irrelevant context, and temporal reordering enforces feasible event sequences. No retriever-aware training or distractor-aware SFT. Limitations section notes the agent can still be biased toward TKG contents and struggle on novel scenarios / incomplete knowledge.
memory_type: graph (temporal knowledge graph World Model) serving as structured episodic/experiential memory; plus a transient within-episode reflection list (R_t) and an inner-monologue working memory (M_t).
write_back: True. Executed transitions (o_t || a_t || o_{t+1}) are summarized, coreference-resolved (Stanford CoreNLP), parsed by an LLM into entity/relation tuples, and added to the TKG as quadruples (v_i, e_j, v_k, tau): G_{t+1} = G_t U {(v_i, e_j, v_k, tau)}. Primary population is during the training phase from golden-trajectory rollouts.
online_growth: Partially/by design. The TKG is described as continuously evolving with the agent's interactions (append of new transition quadruples), so the store can grow as transitions are recorded; however, the reported experimental protocol populates the WM offline from 150 golden-trajectory variations before evaluation, and the inner monologue can dynamically update the WM based on retrieved insights. Whether the graph grows further at test time during the reported ScienceWorld runs is not made fully explicit. [uncertain]
write_back_trigger: On observed transition (per-step append during experience collection): each executed action and its resulting observation are encoded and written to the TKG. Primary writes occur during training-phase golden-trajectory rollouts. Separately, the Critic's reflection list R_t is updated on detected prediction/observation discrepancies (failure-triggered) within an episode, but that is transient replanning context, not a permanent TKG write. Not human-validated.
failure_experience_usage: Experience storage in the TKG is transition-based (observation/action transitions from golden trajectories), not labeled success-vs-failure. Failure handling is via the Critic's within-episode reflection: discrepancies (Delta_t) between predicted and actual outcomes are stored in a reflection list R_t and used as additional context to trigger and guide replanning within the current execution. So failures drive corrective replanning but are not retained as persistent failure cases in the long-term memory.
memory_evolution_update: Append-only growth of the TKG (union of new quadruples with timestamps; coreference resolution merges entity mentions during extraction). No explicit delta-update/forget-prune/refine-overwrite of existing stored facts is described; temporal information is added as timestamped edges so the graph accumulates time-ordered facts. The within-episode reflection list R_t is appended to and reset across executions.
retrieval_as_learned_policy: No. Retrieval/subgraph selection is a fixed prompted graph-QA + heuristic-expansion process (LLM-driven), not a trained or RL-optimized retrieval policy. The agent's action policy itself is an LLM-prompted model-based planner, not an RL-learned retrieval policy.
cross_agent_or_cross_framework_sharing: No. Single-agent private World Model / temporal knowledge graph; no multi-agent or cross-framework memory sharing.
benchmarks: (1) ScienceWorld (Wang et al., 2022): 30 tasks across 9 grade-school science subjects (Matter, Thermodynamics, Electricity, Biology, Botany, Chemistry, Lifespan/Life Stages, Physics, Genetics); 10 interconnected locations, ~200 object types, 25 high-level actions; >100 variations per task; max steps 80 (hyperparameter table lists 100). (2) HotpotQA (Yang et al., 2018) and MusiqueQA / MuSiQue (Trivedi et al., 2022) for multi-hop QA, 400 randomly sampled instances each, following GraphReader (Li et al., 2024)'s protocol.
benchmark_family: embodied/interactive (ScienceWorld) + multi-hop QA (HotpotQA, MusiqueQA). Per the survey's normalized grouping: embodied (ScienceWorld) and QA / multi-hop (HotpotQA, MuSiQue).
baselines: ScienceWorld: SayCan (Ahn et al., 2022), ReAct (Yao et al., 2023), Reflexion (Shinn et al., 2023), RAP (Kagaya et al., 2024). SwiftSage (Lin et al., 2023), the prior ScienceWorld SOTA, was excluded from replication baselines due to code/eval-method discrepancies. For fairness, both RAP and DAVIS used memory built from five episodes of golden trajectories. Multi-hop QA (World Model comparison): GPT-4o, GPT-4-turbo (raw LLM), GraphReader (GPT-4), HOLMES (GPT-4), GraphRAG (GPT-4o-mini); QA baseline numbers are taken from the original papers (best-reported configs), not re-run.
key_metrics: ScienceWorld: task progress score (0-100, % progress toward completion before failure/timeout), averaged across subjects/variations; plus average steps per replanning cycle (steps/replan) in ablations. Multi-hop QA: Exact Match (EM) and F1.
headline_result: On ScienceWorld, DAVIS outperforms all four baselines on 8 of 9 science subjects, achieving an overall average score of 65.06 (~1.8x higher than competing methods). For the World Model on multi-hop QA, DAVIS (GPT-4o) reaches HotpotQA F1 73.8 / EM 56.25 and MusiqueQA F1 48.5 / EM 33.8, surpassing GraphReader and GraphRAG on HotpotQA and approaching the SOTA HOLMES (HotpotQA EM 66.0 / F1 78.0).
ablations: Two ablation tables on representative short/medium/long tasks (3 variations each). (1) World Model ablation (Table 1, DAVIS without WM 'D' vs with WM 'D+W'): WM consistently and often dramatically improves performance, e.g., Melt 1-2 3.00 -> 70.00, Determine Melting Point Unknown 2-3 5.00 -> 92.33, Find Living Thing 4-1 25.00 -> 100.00, Lifespan Longest-Lived 7-1 66.67 -> 100.00; on Mix Paint Secondary 6-1 the WM did not help (40.00 -> 36.37). (2) Actor/Critic ablation (Table 2, full D+W vs no-Actor D-A vs no-Critic D-C): removing the Actor causes invalid-command struggles, low scores, and near-1.0 steps/replan (constant replanning); removing the Critic loses error recovery on long tasks (gap widens on longer tasks needing adaptive reasoning). E.g., long task 2-3: 92.3 (full) vs 79.7 (no-Actor) vs 33.3 (no-Critic); short 4-1: 100 vs 44.7 vs 25. Conclusion: WM supplies temporal/multi-hop grounding, Actor enables valid structured execution, Critic enables adaptivity.
evaluation_decoupling: Partial. For multi-hop QA the World Model is evaluated with intrinsic QA metrics (EM/F1) separately from the end-to-end ScienceWorld task scores, effectively decoupling the retrieval/QA component's quality. However, no standard top-k retrieval metrics (Recall@k / nDCG) are reported for the experience-retrieval step within planning.
process_vs_outcome_metrics: Both. Primary ScienceWorld metric is outcome (task progress score), but the ablation also reports a process metric: average steps per replanning cycle (steps/replan), interpreted as planning coherence/efficiency (higher steps/replan with strong scores = coherent, cost-efficient planning). Multi-hop QA uses outcome metrics (EM/F1).
cost_efficiency_tradeoff: High operational cost is explicitly reported as a limitation: each action involves ~43,000 tokens sent/received due to the structured multi-turn inner-monologue interaction with the TKG, averaging ~$0.43 per action; a 100-action task can scale to ~$43 per episode, totaling over $3,000 across the 90 experimental variations (the GitHub README states the full 90 variations over 30 tasks with GPT-4-turbo cost over $2,000 in credits). Inner-monologue is capped at Maximum QA Turns = 5 and predicted trajectory length = 5 to bound cost. Authors frame this as a deliberate depth-of-reasoning vs efficiency trade-off and propose future distillation/fine-tuning onto smaller open-source models. DAVIS also reportedly converged in fewer steps than SayCan/ReAct/Reflexion.
context_budget_and_selection_count: Bounded by fixed loop/scope caps rather than a token-truncation budget: Maximum QA Turns = 5 (inner-monologue retrieval turns per transition prediction), predicted trajectory length L = 5, retrieval scope limited to two most relevant entities per query (then neighbor-expanded into a maximal subgraph), max steps per task = 80 (hyperparameter table lists 100). Per-action footprint ~43k tokens.
benchmark_construction_and_size: N/A (DAVIS is a method, not a benchmark contribution). It evaluates on existing benchmarks: ScienceWorld (30 tasks / 9 subjects / >100 variations each; 150 training and 90 test variations used), and HotpotQA & MusiqueQA (400 sampled instances each).
builds_on: Model-based planning / world models (Sutton & Barto, 1998; Dreamer-style latent imagination, Hafner et al., 2020; MuZero, Schrittwieser et al., 2020); knowledge-graph world models of textual environments (Ammanabrolu & Riedl, 2021; Ammanabrolu & Hausknecht, 2020), generalized to temporal KGs; temporal-KG forecasting via in-context learning (Lee et al., 2023); graph QA / graph-based retrieval (GraphReader, Li et al., 2024; HOLMES, Panda et al., 2024; GraphRAG, Edge et al., 2024); RAG agentic planning with memory (RAP, Kagaya et al., 2024; Reflexion, Shinn et al., 2023); ReAct (Yao et al., 2023), SayCan (Ahn et al., 2022), SwiftSage (Lin et al., 2023); Stanford CoreNLP (Manning et al., 2014); ScienceWorld (Wang et al., 2022).
contrasts_with: Vector/semantic-search RAG agents with unstructured episodic memory: Reflexion and RAP (nearest-neighbor retrieval of past experiences), which DAVIS argues fragment information and cannot support multi-hop/causal/temporal reasoning and use static (single-shot) retrieval. CoT-only agents (ReAct, SayCan, SwiftSage) lacking long-term structured memory. Static graph-QA systems (HOLMES's static hyper-relational graph) that cannot update during inference, unlike DAVIS's dynamically updating TKG. Positioned as the first RAG agent to employ an interactive (agentic multi-turn) retrieval method within a RAG pipeline.
lineage: Group C (RAG for planning): experience/memory-based planning agents. DAVIS sits in the experience/episodic-memory planner line but replaces flat vector experience retrieval (Reflexion/RAP) with agentic multi-turn graph QA over a temporal knowledge-graph world model, bridging the GraphRAG / graph-QA retrieval line (GraphReader, HOLMES, GraphRAG) with model-based interactive agent planning.
